bib.title: Chapter 3: Exploring LLMs as a Powerful AI Engine (Building AI Agents with LLMs, RAG, and Knowledge Graphs)
bib.venue: Packt (book chapter, O'Reilly online copy printed 12/26/25)

question: How do transformers become LLMs at scale, how are they tuned, shrunk, extended to other modalities and prompted, and what are their limits (hallucination, bias, legal risk)?
contributions: Overview of scaling laws, emergent properties, context length and mixture of experts
Overview of LoRA, adapters, RLHF, DPO and instruction tuning
Overview of quantization, pruning and distillation for smaller LLMs
Overview of ViT, CLIP, BLIP-2 and Stable Diffusion
Overview of hallucination, bias, copyright, privacy and misuse, and of prompting techniques (ICL, CoT, self-consistency, ToT, DSPy)

limits: No experiments of the authors' own; every number is relayed from other work, mostly without a named reference in the sentence.

Several statements conflict with standard accounts: attention is said to hold the most parameters, weights are said to grow with context length, GPT-4 and Gemini are called MoE (unconfirmed by the vendors).
The scaling-law equation, quantization formula and ViT token-count formulas are images or garbled in the text; only the surrounding prose is readable.
Authors concede the emergent-abilities result is contested, that the scaling law depends on architecture and training choices, and that prompt tuning and prefix tuning can be unstable.
Date-sensitive: written for 2024-25 models; the DSPy and MoE remarks have moved on.
practices: Prototype architecture variants on a small proxy model, then scale, since a scaling law predicts loss before training (scaling law section).
Prefer human-written tokens over synthetic ones for pretraining, because of model collapse and forgetting (scaling law section).
Use LoRA or adapters instead of full fine-tuning for very large models; they remain the most widely used PEFT methods (fine-tuning section).
Use DPO to avoid a reward model and reinforcement learning when aligning (alignment section).
Build instruction-tuning sets with a wide variety of tasks, especially reasoning with steps in context (instruction tuning).
Choose a small model (train from scratch, distil, quantize or prune) when a task is narrow (smaller LLMs section).
Detoxify pretraining data, check fine-tuning labels for annotator bias, and vary sources (ethics section).
Measure bias with Hugging Face Evaluate (toxicity, regard) on gender- and occupation-swapped prompts (ethics section).

Use few-shot (3, 5 or 10 examples), chain-of-thought, zero-shot CoT ('Let's think step by step'), self-consistency and tree of thoughts for reasoning, accepting higher compute cost (prompt engineering).
Use DSPy signatures, modules and optimizers to automate prompt search (prompt engineering).

terms.definition: a model that has more than 10 billion parameters
properties that are not present in a small model but emerge in a large model, abruptly at a critical scale
sparse MoE layers of several experts plus a gate network or router that decides which tokens each expert sees
Low-Rank Adaptation: freeze the weights and train two low-rank matrices A and B whose product is the weight update
three steps: supervised fine-tuning, training a reward model from ranked outputs, then PPO with a KL penalty
Direct Preference Optimization: loss on <prompt, worse completion, better completion> that needs no reward model
further training of a pre-trained model on instruction-output pairs to improve task following
mapping the model weights from higher-precision data types to lower-precision ones
removing unnecessary weights, connections or whole layers; unstructured zeroes weights, structured removes neurons, blocks or layers
production of nonsensical or unfaithful content, split into factuality and faithfulness hallucination
performing a new task at inference from examples in the prompt, with no parameter update
adding 'Let's think step by step' to the prompt to elicit intermediate reasoning
